title: dotInsights | 2026 年 8 月
author: Matt Ellis
content:
Did you know? Ever wondered why C# uses the semicolon to terminate a statement? Obviously it comes from the C/C++ heritage it shares with other languages like Java, but where did C get it from? That would be Algol, where the semicolon was used to separate statements. 

But why the semicolon? In natural language grammar, the semicolon separates two independent but related clauses; it can also be used to separate items in a list (see what I did there?). And what is a program but a list of independent but related clauses?

(Bonus punctuation trivia: the comma is used to separate items in a list, just like the arguments in a function call. The period is used to end a complete thought, like a sentence or paragraph. How did Algol mark the end of a program unit? Why yes, with a period!)

🗞️ JetBrains News

What’s going on at JetBrains? Check it out here:

  • We’ve released the 2026.2 wave of dotUltimate tools – Rider 2026.2, with lots of goodies, including new skills and quality check hooks for agents, Hot Reload for WPF, TypeScript 7 support, improved game dev features for Unreal Engine and Godot. ReSharper 2026.2 gets Junie support, as part of our move to an open AI platform thanks to ACP. It also gets out of process mode enabled by default, so most of ReSharper runs outside of the Visual Studio process.
  • ReSharper for Visual Studio Code 2026.2 was released, and now includes the #1 requested feature – debugging! As everyone knows, debugging is only half the story, so read Isaac’s first blog post detailing how ReSharper can help you write C# inside not just VS Code, but all other compatible editors (Cursor, Google Antigravity IDE, Devin Desktop, Kiro, and others). Check it out on the Marketplace or the OpenVSX Registry.
  • We’ve announced our annual gamedev day for September 28. Make sure to save the date, and send us proposals for sessions!
  • And finally, continuing our series of evaluating skills that claim to reduce token usage, we take a look at the Ponytail skill. Does it really reduce agent code by 54%? #QTWTAIN (You can also check out our evaluation of the rtk skill – does it really cut agent tokens by 60-90%? You might be able to guess from the hashtag…)
